subject: Latency commitments for HeliosPay — p50/p95 windows & short-term variance
messages:
From: Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@heliospay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — initial questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward procurement, our legal and SRE teams need a clear statement of latency commitments for the hosted API we intend to rely on. Specifically we want:

- Per-route p50 and p95 commitments (interactive payment flows vs. batch reconciliation)
- How latency is measured (windowing/aggregation semantics)
- Carveouts (deploys, maintenance, regional outages) and how credits are calculated
- Whether we can request a temporary p95 variance during our Q2 onboarding (high burst risk)

I'm attaching a short list of questions the procurement team collated (HeliosPay_SLA_Questions.pdf). Could you share a proposed SLO layout and an example credit calculation? If there are model- or region-specific differences please call those out.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Liao
Head of Procurement, HeliosPay

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — initial questions

Hi Sarah — great to hear from you. Appreciate the deck of questions. Quick answers up front and a proposed SLO draft attached.

High-level proposal (hosted API):
- Traffic classes: interactive (user-facing, < 1s payloads) and batch (async, larger prompts).
- Proposed commitments (per-route, measured at egress from Redwood inference tier):
  • Interactive: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 600ms
  • Batch: p50 <= 350ms, p95 <= 1,400ms
- Measurement windowing: rolling 30-minute windows per route, reported as daily aggregates. SLO is evaluated against daily targets; monthly credit computations use calendar-month aggregation of daily burn.
- Carveouts: scheduled maintenance (not exceeding 2 hours/month), and a 15-minute operational deployment window per service manifest. Regional provider incidents have regional carveouts if we cannot failover (<1% of traffic historically).
- Temporary variance: we are willing to grant a bounded p95 variance (see below) for an onboarding period with explicit remediation and traffic shaping commitments from HeliosPay.

Credit example (summary):
- If monthly availability (per-route p95 compliance) falls below threshold, credits are pro-rated against that route's portion of monthly usage. For a 10% miss across the month we propose a 10% credit of the monthly bill attributable to that route's token usage. Full formula in the attached PDF.

I've attached a compact proposal (redwood-hosted-slo-proposal-v1.pdf) and a short MAP draft. Can you confirm the operational window risk profile (expected Q2 bursts) so we can finalize the temporary variance terms?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:17:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API latency commitments — internal: variance request from HeliosPay

Internal note — forwarding HeliosPay's ask. They want a temporary relax on p95 for the interactive route during a planned Q2 onboarding spike. Key asks:
- 3 month variance window starting Apr 1
- p95 relaxed to 900ms for interactive traffic for first 30 days, then review
- explicit remediation (traffic shaping, burst caps) and telemetry hooks in our Console

My recommended approach: approve a bounded variance with these safeguards:
- Timeboxed (90 days) with checkpoints at 30 and 60 days
- Tie variance to limits: no more than 25% of their traffic may be allowed to exceed baseline p95; otherwise variance revokes
- Include per-incident runbook obligations and a rollback-to-fallback-model clause

Can you both weigh in on technical feasibility (kernel selection/quantization fallbacks) and whether we should require a partial Reserved capacity commitment during the variance?

—Marissa
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API latency commitments — internal: variance request from HeliosPay

Marissa / Lauren — quick tech take:
- We can support a timeboxed p95 variance for interactive traffic, but recommend the following guardrails:
  1) Regional scoping: make the variance apply only to the US region (reduces blast radius).
  2) Measurement window: switch to a rolling 60-minute window for the exception period to avoid noisy short spikes driving credit burns. Outside the variance we keep the 30-minute rolling window.
  3) Fallbacks: we should provision an automatic model-variant fallback (smaller quantized model) when request queue depth exceeds X (we'll set X with SRE). That will preserve throughput but may increase hallucination risk — document it.
  4) Autoscale & pre-warm: require HeliosPay to enable burst reservations or agree to a short Reserved-capacity add-on for the onboarding month(s) to cap cost exposure for Redwood.

Also recommend the variance include an explicit remediation playbook and a monthly review. From a billing perspective, credit computation must use per-route token attribution to avoid cross-route leakage.

If legal wants a simpler phrasing, propose: 'Temporary p95 variance limited to US region, 90-day duration, subject to pre-agreed traffic caps and telemetry integrations.'

—Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the details on the Q2 onboarding pattern. After internal review we can offer the following package to support HeliosPay's go-live while protecting both sides:

Offer summary:
- Standard hosted commitments (per-route):
  • Interactive: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 600ms (measured on a rolling 30-minute window)
  • Batch: p50 <= 350ms, p95 <= 1,400ms (rolling 30-minute window)
- Temporary variance (US region only):
  • Duration: 90 days starting Apr 1 (review at 30 and 60 days)
  • Allowed interim p95 for interactive: up to 900ms
  • Measurement for variance: rolling 60-minute windows to reduce volatility-driven penalties
  • Guardrails: no more than 25% of interactive traffic may exceed baseline p95; automatic model-variant fallback enabled; HeliosPay must enable burst reservations or accept a small Reserved-capacity add-on for the onboarding window.
- Credits: pro-rated monthly credit based on per-route token usage when SLOs are missed. Exact formula in the attached MAP.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached MAP and SLO draft and confirm acceptance of the guardrails.
2) If accepted, we'll issue a short addendum for signature (DocuSign link below).
3) We'll schedule a 30-minute runbook review with your SREs to set thresholds for model fallbacks and queue depth.
